newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Lenzing says no plans to close U.S. plant.
newsitem.headline: Lenzing says no plans to close U.S. plant.

text.p: Austrian fibre maker Lenzing said on Friday a newspaper report about alleged plans to shut down its U.S. operations were "completely without foundation".
Daily Wirtschaftsblatt said the company was about to close its Lenzing Fibres Corp. in Lowland, Tenn., which it acquired in 1992, as market conditions in the U.S. had deteriorated markedly.
"That is nonsense," a company spokeswoman told Reuters. "We expect a positive cash flow from the plant in the current year, and see it almost breaking even in 1998."
She declined to detail how much money the plant had lost last year. Lenzing plans to report its key 1996 earnings data next week.
In March, Lenzing reported a provisional 1996 pretax loss of around 160 million schillings, after a profit of 312.6 million, and warned that earnings were not expected to improve this year.
Lenzing shares were down 5.90 schillings at 695 in early trade on the Vienna stock exchange.
